article.articleSummary: A 14-year-old girl in Xiamen, Fujian, China, presented with persistent lower back pain but no fever. The infection was likely seeded through an invasive procedure performed at a clinic, allowing bacteria to invade the spine. Targeted antibiotics led to rapid pain relief and good recovery on follow-up. The report emphasizes that teenage spinal infections are rare and may present without fever, urging thorough evaluation of persistent or progressive back pain (over ~2 weeks) with ESR and MRI, and caution against early invasive therapies such as acupuncture or local injections. Obtaining tissue for culture is essential to guide precise therapy and prevent chronic complications. Influenza vaccination targets the elderly, children, and pregnant women; rural areas offer a free one-dose vaccine for 65+ and schoolchildren, with some employers running ‘two go, one free’ promos. Avoid crowded indoor spaces; keep homes ventilated daily and wear masks outdoors. Varicella spreads by droplets and vesicle fluid; vaccinate eligible individuals, isolate until crusting, trim nails, wash hands, and avoid sharing utensils. Scarlet fever requires proper antibiotic treatment and follow-up to prevent nephritis and rheumatic fever. Scrub typhus peaks Oct–Nov; avoid dense shrubs, keep dry, wear light clothing, use repellents, and shower after outdoor activity. HFRS is endemic; reduce rodent exposure, seal entryways, store grains securely, and vaccinate 16–60-year-olds. Also heed carbon monoxide poisoning risk.

article.articleHeadline: Hunan CDC reminds: In November, the risk of these two types of diseases is high.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-11-03, Hunan Province, China, the CDC released the November 2026 disease risk forecast, highlighting two highest-risk conditions: Acute Respiratory Infections (risk level II, high) and Norovirus Gastroenteritis (risk level III, medium). With temperatures dropping toward the winter solstice, authorities urge vigilance for ARIs, whose symptoms include fever, headache, myalgia, cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, and runny nose. Preventive measures include vaccination, masking in public, ventilation by opening windows, diligent hand hygiene, and proper cough etiquette. For Norovirus Gastroenteritis, symptoms are abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting; preventives emphasize good personal hygiene, food hygiene with separating raw and cooked foods, avoiding untreated water, indoor ventilation, and seeking timely medical care if ill. I–IV levels denote high, relatively high, medium, and low risk, respectively.

article.articleHeadline: Attention! Influenza in Sichuan has reached a moderate level of epidemic activity, and in some areas the meteorological risk of influenza is relatively high.
article.articleSummary: As of 3 November 2026, influenza activity in Sichuan Province, China, has reached a moderate level, with overall influenza meteorological risk rising in parts of the province. The Sichuan Meteorological Bureau and Sichuan Center for Disease Control and Prevention jointly released a five-tier influenza meteorological risk forecast (low, lower, moderate, higher, high) to guide prevention. October detected medium-level circulation, and November is projected to continue elevated risk. Expected for November: average temperature 11.4–11.9°C (above the long-term 10.9°C) and precipitation 20–25 mm (near 22.8 mm). The month may see four cooling–rainfall episodes, with a transmission peak 1–3 days around cold fronts. A notable period is forecast for 6–8 November, when most basins experience light rain, the southwestern and southern areas may see moderate rain, and daily average temperatures could drop 2–4°C. Health risk advisories accompany the forecast.

The president welcomed the fence buildup as a positive development for disease risk management, while Jung stressed readiness for coordinated quarantine. He added that wild boars have historically crossed the Amrok (Yalu) and Tumen rivers, and warned that budgetary pre-planning is essential in light of past livestock culling and leachate issues. This signals ongoing cross-border veterinary cooperation.

article.articleHeadline: The legal, trade and compliance implications of the FMD outbreak
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak in Namibia's Karas Region, within the WOAH-recognised FMD-free zone around Karasburg, prompted suspension of Namibia’s FMD-free status and halting of exports to South Africa, the European Union, China and the United States. Confirmed on 23 September 2026, the outbreak remains localized within Karas as of 3 November 2026, with some restrictions partially lifted. Farmers must report suspected cases immediately, observe movement limits, quarantine, and enhanced biosecurity, while independent vaccination outside the DVS is discouraged. Authorities emphasize traceability (animal IDs, movement records, farm registers) to map transmission. Containment is estimated at about N$190.2 million, including N$47 million for 290 km of fencing Ariamsvlei–Karasburg–Ai-Ais; the FMD Support Fund has mobilised over N$1.5 million in biosecurity products and equipment. Botswana-inspired, regional cooperation and risk-based controls are highlighted as essential to restoring market access and confidence.

article.articleHeadline: As bird flu spreads, dairy industry awaits vaccine | Capital Press
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza (bird flu) continues to spread among U.S. dairy cattle, with about 40 Washington dairies infected and a Yakima County resident who exposed to sick cattle dying on Nov. 1. Nationwide, 1,222 herds in 21 states have been affected since March 2024, despite milk testing and movement controls, as the industry weighs trade impacts and control tools. The outbreak traces to wild birds and poultry; cattle became a concern after a 2024 Texas dairy outbreak. USDA has not licensed a cattle vaccine, though several candidates are in field trials as it solicits developers. A Oct. 28 nature.com study by University of Pennsylvania and USDA showed four Holstein cows vaccinated mounted an immune response with no adverse effects. Nebraska researchers vaccinated mice and calves (April), and the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences reported protection in a small number of cows (January). Washington dairy leaders warn licensing decisions could affect markets while expanding disease-control options.

article.articleHeadline: Researchers Identify Antibodies Linked to Severe Viral Infections
article.articleSummary: Antibodies that block type I interferons raise risk of severe viral infections, including severe COVID-19. Karolinska Institutet researchers identify the B cells that produce these autoantibodies and map their development, with findings published in the Journal of Experimental Medicine on 2026-11-03. In severe COVID-19 patients, the neutralizing antibodies mainly originate from memory B cells; in APS-1 patients, they are predominantly found in atypical B cells linked to long-term immune activation. By analyzing blood samples from severe COVID-19 patients and individuals with APS-1, the team elucidates the cellular origin of these antibodies, potentially aiding diagnostics and new treatments for viral diseases. Collaborations spanned Uppsala University (Sweden), Peking University (China), Università della Svizzera italiana (Switzerland), Karolinska University Hospital, and partner institutions in Italy; funding from Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, Swedish Research Council, EU Horizon 2020, and Nordstjernan. Potential patents for diagnostics and therapeutics against type I interferons are being considered.

The southern region is more active (over 600 clusters) than the north (about 200). Week 43 surveillance shows COVID-19 as the top pathogen among acute respiratory infections, with multiple co-circulating strains and possible concurrent influenza and myocarditis. article.articleHeadline: Dengue Fever Outbreak Hits Construction Sites in China's Hainan, Thousands of Workers Quarantined
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever outbreak at several high-end residential construction sites in Sanya, Hainan, has led to thousands placed under quarantine and construction halted. Dozens infected; estimated 4,000–5,000 workers affected across multiple sites in the Jiyang District, including the Sanya Poly Tianjun project. Hundreds relocated to the Sanya Evergrande Beauty Crown residential complex and the Beauty Crown Hotel for quarantine and testing; about 800–1,000 workers per site affected. Authorities deployed environmental disinfection and mosquito-control measures, including ground spraying and drones. Some workers were hospitalized; officials have not released precise case counts. The outbreak was reported October 31, with police at site entrances and the mayor visiting; lockdowns caused wage and job disruption due to suspended work. Dengue is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; incubation 1–14 days; symptoms include fever, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain; severe forms possible.

article.articleHeadline: 1918 - Spanish flu kills 36 people in Campo Grande.
article.articleSummary: Spanish flu outbreak in Campo Grande, Brazil, reported on 3 November 1918 by mayor Rosário Congro. Despite being labeled benign, the pandemic spread rapidly, reaching Campo Grande and rural towns such as Entre Rios, Jaraguari, and Rio Pardo, with the city recording over 1,000 notified cases and more than 2,000 across the municipality. The death toll in Campo Grande was 36. Due to a lack of prophylaxis and adequate hospital facilities, the city functioned as a large hospital, organizing ambulatory care in the municipal school building; six patients were hospitalized and an early death occurred in a shack. Resources dwindled—pharmacy closures and shortages of milk and poultry—prompting about 150 municipal prescriptions and redistribution of supplies. A quinine donation from Dr. Antonio Ferrari arrived as the epidemic declined, later shared with Corumbá’s mayor, Dr. Nicolau Fragelli. Hygiene delegate Dr. José Gentil da Silva led care and home visits. Total municipal expenditure: 4:658$300 as of 30 April 1918.

article.articleHeadline: Panel Allows Monitoring of Babies' Protection Against a Respiratory Virus.
article.articleSummary: Brazil's Ministry of Health launched a nationwide RSV protection monitoring panel to track immunity among premature babies and other vulnerable children. The platform records nirsevimabe administration, an antibody used to prevent severe Respiratory Syncytial Virus disease, enabling health managers to monitor coverage, identify regions with lower protection, and plan targeted outreach. It supports epidemiological surveillance for rapid responses to rising cases or outbreaks. Data come from the National Health Data Network and the Live Birth Information System, integrated to reduce registration gaps and inform states and municipalities. RSV is a leading cause of infant respiratory infections and can require hospitalization, especially for preterm infants or those with certain conditions. Nirsevimabe is indicated for infants up to 36 weeks and 6 days gestation, regardless of birth weight, and for children up to two years with risk factors such as congenital heart disease, Down syndrome, cystic fibrosis, neuromuscular diseases, or immunodeficiency. Data are openly accessible to managers, professionals, civil society, and the public, increasing transparency in SUS immunization data.

article.articleHeadline: Marine animal deaths surge 120% in Florianópolis and trigger warnings of disease contamination on beaches.
article.articleSummary: Florianópolis, Santa Catarina, Brazil, reports a 120% year-over-year rise in marine animal deaths along its beaches, prompting warnings of potential infectious disease contamination for beachgoers and dogs. Investigations, aired by SC No Ar and conducted by the Associação R3 Animal (South America’s largest marine rehabilitation center), show necropsies and lab analyses on penguins, sea turtles, and seabirds, with plastics, fishing hooks, and nets identified as key death drivers. Most affected animals are juveniles; causes include drowning in gear, malnutrition, ingestion of debris, natural stress, parasites, and low immunity. Authorities urge people to keep distance from carcasses and never touch them, given the risk of transmitting infectious agents to humans and pets. For debilitated or dead animals, contact environmental agencies and rescue teams. The center also rescues, rehabilitates, and uses radiography/ultrasound for diagnosis, releasing healthy animals back into the wild after recovery.

article.articleHeadline: Bats Spread a Silent Threat to Agriculture - Boca do Povo News
article.articleSummary: Rabies detected in cattle across Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, with 66 herbivore samples testing positive from January to September 2026. Hematophagous bats are among the main transmitters. Rabies can incubate for months before symptoms appear, at which point the disease is often established in the herd. Infected animals may show difficulty walking, apathy, loss of appetite, and excessive salivation. Farmers are advised not to touch suspected animals and to report immediately to the Agricultural Defense agency (Defesa Agropecuária). Rabies has no cure and can infect humans, underscoring the need for prevention on farms, as even nocturnal flying animals can pose a risk. The report adds to ongoing concerns among producers about input costs, weather, and market conditions.

article.articleSummary: Paraíso do Tocantins launches the second cycle of the Good Collar Project to prevent visceral leishmaniasis (calazar) in dogs. Upcoming sessions include early November in Aeroporto and Interlagos, with additional dates through November and December in sectors Vale do Araguaia, Milena, Jardim Paulista, and others. Participants must bring photo ID, proof of address, and the animal vaccination card. For more information, contact UVCZ at (63) 99952-9973.

article.articleHeadline: The Brazil You Don't See: The Challenge of Neglected Tropical Diseases
article.articleSummary: Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) in Brazil comprise a broad group including viral, bacterial, and parasitic diseases that disproportionately affect vulnerable populations with limited health access. Dengue, chikungunya, leprosy (Hansen’s disease), schistosomiasis, and trachoma are discussed, with current hotspots in the North, Northeast, and Central-West regions; climate change and vector mobility threaten spread to other areas. Despite available diagnostics, treatments, and cures for most NTDs, underinvestment in research and new medicines persists, constraining progress. The episode features scientist Dr. Sebastian Vernal and patient Marilza Osório, a 54-year-old in Rio Branco, Acre, who endured a five-year delay before a leprosy diagnosis. Leprosy is a bacterial, infectious disease marked by skin patches with altered sensation and nerve pain. The interview emphasizes awareness, treatment, rights, and the need for better funding and access in Brazil.

article.articleSummary: RSV vaccination for pregnant women in Atibaia is provided free by the SUS to those from 28 weeks of gestation, with one dose per pregnancy. Maternal antibodies are transferred to the newborn, helping protect against severe respiratory illness in the first six months. The program follows a national Ipsos-Ipec survey for Pfizer, which found 530 pregnant women aged 18–45 with 79% reporting doubts about RSV and its prevention; bronchiolitis was cited as a top concern by 60%; while 70% had heard of RSV, only 13% answered all questions correctly. Vaccination in Atibaia began December 2025 and was incorporated into UBSs in 2026. To receive the dose, pregnant women should present photo ID, prenatal or gestational card, proof of gestational age, and vaccination card at the nearest UBS.

article.articleHeadline: The 2027 flu vaccine will include H1N1 and H3N2 strains.
article.articleSummary: Brazil's immunization program for February 1, 2027 will include influenza vaccine strains H1N1, H3N2, and Victoria lineage B. Egg-based vaccines will contain A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09, A/Darwin/1454/2025 (H3N2), and B/1359417/2021 Victoria; labels will read 'Strains 2027 Southern Hemisphere'. Non-egg vaccines will use A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09, A/Darwin/1454/2025 (H3N2), and B/Pennsylvania/14/2025 Victoria; IN 475/2026 published by Anvisa. Some Health Ministry campaigns in Brazil may use Northern Hemisphere 2026-2027 vaccines in specific regions with strains A/Missouri/11/2025, A/Darwin/1454/2025 (H3N2), and B/Tokyo/EIS13-175/2025 Victoria, labeled 'Strains 2026-2027 Northern Hemisphere'. Annual reformulation is due to influenza's rapid mutation and waning immunity; WHO surveillance informs strains; vaccination remains essential to reduce complications and severe disease.

article.articleHeadline: As the weather changes, the risk of influenza A increases; learn preventive measures from a doctor.
article.articleSummary: Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh, India — as weather changes, eye flu (conjunctivitis) cases are rising. Ophthalmologist Dr. Manisha Singh notes symptoms: redness, itching, pain, and watery discharge. Preventive measures include thorough handwashing, not sharing towels or kajal, and avoiding eye drops without medical advice. If one family member is infected, others are at risk; emphasize home cleanliness and hand hygiene to limit spread. Those with infection should wear protective eyewear and refrain from touching the eyes. Do not use eye drops purchased from a store without doctor consultation; do not share used eye drops. Eye flu can be bacterial or viral; bacterial cases may respond to doctor-prescribed antibiotic eye drops. Eye drops opened should only be used for up to one month. Public recommendations include avoiding sharing with infected individuals and maintaining personal hygiene in public places.

article.articleHeadline: Drug-Resistant Brain TB in Children: Early Diagnosis to Prevent Neurological Damage
article.articleSummary: Drug-resistant brain tuberculosis (CNS TB) in children in India, highlighted by Dr. Sulakshna Dahiya of Kailash Hospital, Greater Noida, poses diagnostic and treatment challenges. CNS TB, including tuberculous meningitis and brain tuberculomas, risks permanent neurological damage if diagnosed late; drug resistance complicates regimens due to the need for effective CNS penetration. Warning signs span headaches, vomiting, fever, excessive sleepiness, irritability, behavioral changes, convulsions, limb weakness, visual disturbances, and altered consciousness; in young children, poor feeding, lethargy, developmental delay, and motor dysfunction may prevail. Diagnosis relies on clinical examination, MRI/CT imaging, CSF analysis, and microbiological or molecular tests, with mandatory drug-resistance testing. Treatment is prolonged and requires ensuring CNS drug delivery, adherence, and multidisciplinary care. Complications can include hydrocephalus, seizures, cerebrovascular issues, cranial nerve dysfunction, and raised intracranial pressure, impacting cognition and development. A collaborative approach among pediatricians, neurologists, infectious disease specialists, radiologists, microbiologists, and rehabilitation therapists with vigilant monitoring is advised.

He was to travel to Delhi after November 15 for a kidney transplant; a donor was finalised, but the trip is postponed.

article.articleHeadline: Diwali Sweet Boxes: Can Improper Storage Turn Festive Treats Into Food Poisoning Risks?
article.articleSummary: A Scientific Reports study tested Mohanthal stored at 30°C for 20 days in four packaging types: P-1 LDPE thin plastic pouches, P-2 hard plastic tubs, P-3 laminated plastic/foil, and P-4 cardboard boxes. Sweets remained acceptable for 16 days in P-1 and P-4, 20 days in P-2 and P-3; by day 22 visible mold appeared in all. Laminated pouches offered the strongest protection, plastic tubs were good, cardboard the weakest, with moisture around 8.0–9.5%, hardness shifting, and fat spoilage markers lower in laminated packaging. Milk-based sweets like rasgulla are particularly delicate due to milk proteins; warm, humid conditions accelerate spoilage, and E. coli has been detected in some rasgulla samples, with yeast/mold observed in Hyderabad and Secunderabad. Khoa-based sweets last 3–5 days at room temperature and 7–10 days refrigerated, about 2–3 days at small retailers; India produces ~1.5 million tonnes of khoa annually, requiring ~5 kg of milk per 1 kg of khoa. Eat fresh and keep cold when possible.

article.articleHeadline: Maharashtra To Install 300 Advanced TB Diagnostic Machines Under ₹41.92 Crore Project
article.articleSummary: Maharashtra will install 300 advanced Truenat Quattro molecular diagnostic machines across the state to boost tuberculosis detection under a Rs 41.92 crore project implemented over 21 months. Deployed at primary health centres, rural hospitals and district-level health institutions under the National TB Elimination Programme, the portable, battery-operated devices can detect TB and Rifampicin-resistant TB within an hour. The initiative, approved by the World Health Organization, will enable about 9.36 lakh tests annually and is expected to identify around 1.12 lakh TB patients and 4,680 Rifampicin-resistant TB cases each year. A tripartite MoU has been signed among the BPCL Foundation, HITES-HLL Infra Tech Services Ltd (implementing agency), and the Joint Director of Health Services (TB and Leprosy). Training for healthcare workers and digital monitoring via the Nikshay platform will accompany rollout to improve access in remote and rural Maharashtra.

article.articleHeadline: Hepatitis B, C A Concern In AP; Estimates Reveal Over 10 Lakh Patients
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis B and C are a growing public health concern in Andhra Pradesh (AP), with estimates that over 2% of the state’s ~5 crore population are infected—more than 10 lakh people. B and C types are prioritized due to risk of chronic liver disease. Central and state authorities have intensified prevention, including a three-dose Hepatitis B vaccination programme covering about 3.69 lakh people across districts. Districts with higher case loads include NTR, East Godavari, Visakhapatnam, Kurnool, and Nellore. High-risk groups comprise sex workers, MSM, people living with HIV, and children born to infected mothers; vaccination is being extended to people born before 2004, since Hep B vaccine was not in routine immunisation until then. Emphasis on early diagnosis to prevent complications, with ongoing measures under the National Hepatitis B Control Programme to reduce cases in coming years.

article.articleHeadline: Anti-filaria drive for 6.7L people in 4 blocks from Nov 19
article.articleSummary: Kanpur district will administer anti-filarial medicines to about 6.77 lakh eligible individuals under the National Filaria Eradication Programme in Bilhaur, Kakwan, Chaubepur and Bidhanu blocks from Nov 19 to Dec 7. The Mass Drug Administration campaign aims to prevent filariasis, a disease transmitted by Culex mosquitoes. Filariasis is caused by microscopic parasites that enter the body after being bitten by an infected mosquito; the parasites can live 5 to 15 years and damage the lymphatic system, causing swelling of arms, legs, or genitals and lifelong disability. Symptoms may appear after many years, so eligible people—healthy-looking ones too—should take the prescribed medicines during the campaign. Training for 85 CHOs online was provided by State Filaria Officer Dr AK Chaudhary. District Malaria Officer AK Singh said 90 supervisors and 1,084 drug distributors have been deployed; preparations are nearly complete.

article.articleHeadline: Four deaths raise concern; fifth fever on the rise.
article.articleSummary: Four measles-related deaths; fifth fever on the rise in Kerala as of October 2026. Kannur, Malappuram, and Kozhikode districts report rising cases, with 538 confirmed measles infections statewide through October and hundreds showing symptoms. In Malappuram and Kozhikode, cases exceed 160 each. A 15-year-old student from Thalassery died after exposure during a school excursion to Kodaikanal; four other students in the group were infected. Health authorities are intensifying surveillance and vaccination drives. Lower vaccination coverage in northern districts correlates with higher transmission; at-risk groups—unvaccinated children, pregnant women, and those with weakened immunity—are at greater risk for severe disease. Measles symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and rash later. Government health centers offer free vaccination: first MR dose at 9-12 months, second dose at 16-24 months, to prevent outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: Rats and Pinjal, Two Vectors of Plague Transmission.
article.articleSummary: Plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, is transmitted through rats and rat fleas, notably Xenopsylla cheopis, which parasitize rodents. Three trophic levels—rats, rat fleas, and the bacteria—drive transmission: when an infected rat dies, fleas seek new hosts and can bite humans, introducing the pathogen. While the Black Death devastated Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia in 1347–1351, today plague in Indonesia is limited to several districts on Java and is under ongoing surveillance by the Ministry of Health. Because rats are central to transmission, controlling rodents in residential areas—through sanitation and removing food sources such as trash—remains a key preventive measure. These points were highlighted by IPB University expert Dr Swastiko Priyambodo in statements cited by Liputan6.com.

article.articleHeadline: Pangkalpinang City Government Strengthens Collaboration in TB, Malaria, and HIV Control.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-11-03, Pangkalpinang City Government in Kepulauan Bangka Belitung strengthened cross-sector and cross-program collaboration to advance AIDS, tuberculosis (TB), and malaria (ATMH) control. The meeting at Grand Safran Hotel reviewed the integration of ATMH services into primary service delivery (ILP) and evaluated ATMH program implementation. Deputy Mayor Dessy Ayutrisna attended; Mayor Saparudin joined remotely via Zoom, with the Health Department chief Dr. Hisar also present. Officials stressed that infectious disease control requires broader engagement beyond the health sector and must reach communities through integrated services at puskesmas, posyandu, health cadres, and local kelurahan administrations. Dr. Hisar cited a malaria case in a traveler from a malaria-endemic area, illustrating the need for early detection and rapid response to prevent local transmission. The initiative aims to strengthen cross-sector coordination for prevention, detection, and treatment of ATMH.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue Fever Case in Batam Kills a 7-Year-Old Child, Three Infants Also Infected Throughout 2026.
article.articleSummary: Dengue Fever (DBD) in Batam, Indonesia, records 570 cases and one death (a 7-year-old child) from January–October 2026, with three infant cases under 1 year old. As of 31 October 2026, Batam has seen a broader outbreak linked to environmental cleanliness gaps, insufficient adherence to Clean and Healthy Living Behaviors (PHBS), and the transitional pancaroba season. Authorities urge residents to maintain hygiene, keep surroundings clean, and seek prompt medical evaluation for fever. Public health measures include Mayor Circular No. 8/2026 on early dengue warning, 3M Plus, and the One House One Jumantik (G1R1J) program. Education continues at puskesmas, posyandu, and schools, complemented by community gotong royong. Fogging is carried out within a 100-meter radius of confirmed cases, after obtaining agreement from RTs/neighborhood groups to conduct mosquito-nest elimination (PSN).

article.articleHeadline: Sorong Regency Government – UB Expedition Team Formulates Malaria Elimination Strategy.
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Sorong Regency, Southwest Papua, Indonesia, spurred collaboration between the Sorong Regency Government and Universitas Brawijaya's Patriot 15 Expedition Team to forge an accelerated elimination strategy after malaria cases rose from 1,100 in 2025 to 1,327 by end-2026. Deputy Regent Sutejo praised the UB team's research and urged rapid translation of recommendations to the Health Department and concrete programs, stressing cross-agency and community involvement to meet the national malaria elimination target by 2030. Health Office Head Agustinus Wabia outlined focal districts with high transmission: Aimas (Klabinain, Maibo), Mayamuk (Jeflio, Arar), Mega (Salawati Selatan, Seget). Interventions center on active case finding, diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and mass bed-net distributions to high-risk villages; ongoing mosquitoes’ habitat control and larval source management; fogging is under study pending socialization and timing around 18:00 WIT. The plan emphasizes village-level engagement and multi-sector support.

article.articleHeadline: Expand Livestock Protection, Tulungagung Ramps Up Foot-and-Mouth Disease Vaccination
article.articleSummary: On 3 November 2026, the Tulungagung Regency government in Indonesia held a foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) vaccination campaign for cattle, goats, and buffalo to celebrate the regency’s 821st anniversary. The drive aims to expand vaccination coverage, strengthen herd immunity, and minimize the risk of FMD spreading among livestock. By boosting animal health, the initiative supports sustainable farming and the livelihoods of local livestock producers in Tulungagung. Authorities frame the program as a preventive measure to protect productivity and the regional economy from potential outbreaks. The effort underscores ongoing engagement in veterinary public health and agricultural development, aligning with broader policies to safeguard livestock health and maintain supply chains for meat and dairy from the district.

article.articleHeadline: Nabire Health Office finds 322 leprosy cases in 2026 - ANTARA News Central Papua
article.articleSummary: Leprosy in Nabire Regency, Central Papua, Indonesia: 322 cases reported in 2026 with 197 undergoing treatment as of July 2026; data updated quarterly and extending to October. New Case Detection Rate (NCDR) 190.38; prevalence 16.38; Release From Treatment (RFT) 18.63. Gender distribution: 59.63% male, 40.37% female. Multibacillary (MB) leprosy accounted for 137 cases in 2025; 84 MB cases identified through Q3 2026. Most cases from three health centers: Sanoba Health Center (47), Kalibobo (44), Siriwini (44). All health facilities have trained program officers for early detection per Ministry of Health standards. Public health messaging urges reducing stigma and supporting patients to complete multidrug therapy. Symptoms include hypopigmented patches with reduced sensation; PB treatment lasts six months, MB twelve months; daily medication with adherence supervision. Pediatric cases highlighted due to household transmission risk.

article.articleHeadline: Nabire Health Office records 1,700 TB cases detected through September 2026 - ANTARA News Central Papua
article.articleSummary: Nabire, Central Papua, records 1,700 tuberculosis cases detected through September 2026, about 70% of the 2,436-case target and below the 90% goal. The five leading health centers—Puskesmas Bumi Wonorejo (202), Karang Tumaritis (181), Kalibobo (109), Siriwini (106), and Samabusa (86)—account for most detections. TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, mainly affecting the lungs, and spreads via airborne droplets from coughing, sneezing, or talking. Symptoms include a cough longer than three weeks, shortness of breath, chest pain, fever, night sweats, weight loss, and fatigue. Diagnosis relies on sputum testing by Tes Cepat Molekuler (TCM) rapid molecular testing. Treatment for drug-susceptible TB lasts six months; drug-resistant TB can require 18–20 months. Adherence remains a challenge; the Find, Treat, Cure (TOS TB) campaign, with medication-administration support, emphasizes early detection and free medicines at puskesmas to prevent transmission.

article.articleHeadline: IPB Discovers an Antimicrobial Resistance Gene in Escherichia coli in the Animal Slaughter Ecosystem.
article.articleSummary: IPB University’s School of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences identified an antimicrobial resistance (AMR) gene in Escherichia coli from the animal slaughter ecosystem in Banten Province, Indonesia. Using whole-genome sequencing, the study found resistance genes across samples from animal, environment, and human sources, covering 12 antibiotic classes. Multidrug resistance (MDR) was observed in 90% of animal isolates, 40% of environmental isolates, and 12.7% of human isolates. About 85% of resistance genes in animal and environmental isolates resided on plasmids, signaling high potential for horizontal transfer. The mcr-1.1 gene, linked to colistin resistance, was detected in 2023 but not in 2026, consistent with reduced colistin use in animals. The findings highlight One Health integration and the need for prudent antibiotic use to curb resistance spread across animal–environment–human interfaces.

article.articleHeadline: Measles outbreaks have appeared in many parts of the world; authorities urge residents to take preventive measures.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreaks are reported globally, prompting Hong Kong to urge preventive measures. In the United States this year, more than 4,800 measles cases have been recorded, with deaths in Pennsylvania and New York among the unvaccinated. Indonesia, Bangladesh, Laos, and the Philippines report outbreaks linked to low vaccination coverage. Hong Kong has 9 cases so far this year: 6 imported or linked, 3 local. The Centre for Health Protection says two-dose measles vaccine coverage among schoolchildren, and overall immunisation in Hong Kong remains above 95%, and local measles antibody seropositivity indicates substantial immunity, making large domestic outbreaks unlikely. However, as an international travel hub, imported cases remain a threat. Unvaccinated groups (new immigrants, domestic workers, overseas workers, and inbound students) risk transmitting to infants under one year. Those born before 1967 are immune; those born in 1967 or later without two doses should complete vaccination.

article.articleHeadline: Acute Respiratory Infections in Timor Tengah Utara Regency Reach 60 Cases in 2026

Preventive measures include adequate rest, vitamin intake, and wearing masks when outdoors. Public health guidance stresses maintaining clean, healthy living and staying hydrated with boiled water; parents are advised to supervise children to avoid indiscriminate street food. The report comes from Kefamenanu, TTU, on November 3, 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Hà Tĩnh strengthens surveillance and prevention of the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola prevention intensified in Ha Tinh Province, Vietnam, on 3 November 2026. The Ha Tinh Department of Health via the CDC Ha Tinh escalates global Ebola surveillance, risk assessment of importation at border gates and seaports, and upstream planning for prevention and control. CDC Ha Tinh directs health facilities to enhance surveillance, screen suspected cases, and train staff on diagnosis, treatment, and infection prevention. Public communications target travelers at borders and the public. Healthcare facilities at district and commune levels are required to take thorough epidemiological histories for returnees from endemic areas or contacts of suspected cases, maintain infection prevention protocols, ensure PPE, and prepare for incident management of suspected cases. Upon detection of a suspected case, facilities must immediately notify CDC Ha Tinh for coordinated response and to prevent nosocomial transmission. Regular updates and adherence to reporting guidelines are emphasized.

article.articleHeadline: Bronchiolitis obliterans after respiratory syncytial virus infection.
article.articleSummary: 19-month-old Mia in Hanoi developed post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans (PIBO) after a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. She previously received treatment in New Zealand but persistent symptoms prompted evaluation at Tam Anh Hanoi Hospital, where chest imaging showed right upper lobe consolidation, bilateral hazy opacities, thickened bronchi walls, and mucus retention. PIBO follows lower respiratory infection in early life; pathogens include RSV, adenovirus, influenza, parainfluenza, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. RSV can injure bronchial epithelium, triggering chronic inflammation and fibrosis with airway obstruction. Unlike acute viral bronchiolitis, PIBO presents with cough, wheeze, tachypnea or dyspnea that persist for months and may lead to bronchiectasis or atelectasis. Diagnosis relies on history and imaging; high-resolution CT can detect small-airway injury and air trapping. No cure exists; treatment focuses on symptom control, infection management, airway clearance, nutrition, and pulmonary follow-up. After 10 days, Mia improved and was discharged; follow-up and avoidance of unnecessary antibiotics or steroids were advised.

article.articleHeadline: Early signs of hand, foot, and mouth disease.
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) is an enterovirus infection, most common in children under 5. EV71 infections can progress to severe neurological, cardiac, or respiratory complications. After a 3–7 day incubation, early symptoms include fever 38–39°C, irritability, fatigue, drooling, sore throat, and mild rhinorrhea or abdominal pain/diarrhea. Within days, painful mouth ulcers and red blisters appear on the hands and feet (palms and fingers). Transmission starts about 2 days before rash and is strongest in the first week; the virus can be shed in stool for around 4 weeks. Dehydration is a key risk due to mouth ulcers. Severe signs warrant hospital care: altered consciousness, high or persistent fever, vomiting, lethargy, limb weakness, or rapid breathing. Treatment is supportive; no specific antiviral or antibiotics; ensure hydration, provide soft foods, and maintain hygiene and home isolation.

article.articleHeadline: Congratulations! Data From WHO COVID-19 Dashboard Shows That Thailand is the Global Hub for SARS-CoV-2 Infections!
article.articleSummary: Thailand accounts for about 62 percent of globally reported SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) cases in the 28 days ending October 11, 2026, with roughly 38,400 of 61,916 worldwide, per the WHO COVID-19 dashboard. The United Kingdom follows with ~7,700 cases. The dashboard uses country-submitted data, and differences in testing, reporting, case definitions, and surveillance systems complicate interpretation; Thailand’s limited testing and sparse public updates hinder assessment of true transmission. The data raise questions about disease surveillance, transparency, and cross-border risk as Thailand remains a major international tourism hub. While infected travelers can spread SARS-CoV-2, asserting that most international cases originate from Thailand requires genomic epidemiology and coordinated surveillance, which are currently lacking. Calls for transparency include testing volumes, positivity, hospitalizations, deaths, variants, and sequencing; and awareness that mild infections can progress to long-term complications such as Long COVID.

article.articleHeadline: 23-year-old Australian influencer on a Bali trip contracts meningitis and is in critical condition; check the illness risk when traveling in Southeast Asia.
article.articleSummary: 23-year-old Australian fitness influencer Khiana Smith contracted meningitis while holidaying in Bali, Indonesia, and remains in critical condition nine days later as of 2026-11-03, after ICU care and treatment for suspected bacterial meningitis followed by pneumonia and pleural effusion. The infection’s exact source is unknown. Meningitis can spread via respiratory droplets or contaminated food, highlighting travel risks in Southeast Asia, with travel-related nervous-system infections reported in the region (notably Thailand). Hong Kong public-health notes advise considering meningococcal vaccination for at-risk travelers and taking precautions such as masks in crowded spaces. article.articleHeadline: Ontario's top doctors traced a measles outbreak through 13 ICU cases with viral sequencing -- the weapon that cracked it -- BigGo Finance
article.articleSummary: Ontario, Canada, measles outbreak traced to a wedding in a neighboring province where an attendee carried measles from Thailand. It became Canada’s largest outbreak in nearly three decades, erasing measles elimination status. By October 2026, hundreds were hospitalized, 13 admitted to intensive care, 50–51 pregnant women infected, and one infant died. The origin was a wedding exposure; infected individuals returned home and spread to households. In most of Ontario, high population immunity halted spread, but transmission surged in a few communities with very low vaccination rates—notably Anabaptist groups that had not seen measles in over 25 years. Pre-pandemic vaccine uptake had drifted downward, and pandemic misinformation further eroded trust. Case definitions began at the wedding link, then broadened; crucially, National Microbiology Laboratory genomic sequencing linked sporadic cases to the outbreak, enabling counting of linked cases. The outbreak was declared over in October 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Doctors have reported maggots in the mouths, noses and tracheostomies of ventilated ICU patients -- including more than 100 larvae removed from one Filipino farmer
article.articleSummary: ICU-acquired myiasis (maggot infestation) is documented in 38 published cases, predominantly affecting the mouth, nose or throat of mechanically ventilated patients; Lucilia sericata accounts for about 45%. In a Swiss ICU, a 78-year-old man intubated for heart surgery developed 13 live larvae in the mouth 60 hours after admission, identified as Lucilia sericata—likely during a midsummer heat wave; larvae were removed and oral care intensified. A Philippine report from Iloilo City details a 71-year-old farmer with laryngeal cancer treated by tracheostomy and cobalt radiation who developed pneumonia; five days pre-admission he bled around the tracheostomy, and surgeons removed more than 100 Sarcophaga flesh flies larvae, 13–14 mm long. Other historical cases include 1998 US ICU patients with nasal maggots after a mouse infestation and 2015 Iran case with eight larvae on the tongue. Underreporting and summer heat as drivers are noted; treatment is usually simple.

article.articleHeadline: Why Do We Still Have Malaria? Everyday Practices Undermining Ghana's Fight Against the Disease
article.articleSummary: Ghana's malaria challenge persists as of 3 November 2026 despite investments in nets, testing, medicines and education. Malaria remains a major public-health burden; transmission is driven by mosquitoes and by poor sanitation, inconsistent net use, self-medication, and limited community participation. Blocked gutters, discarded containers and other water collections create mosquito breeding sites when left unmanaged. Net ownership is insufficient without consistent use, especially by children and pregnant women who are most vulnerable. Self-medication and skipping testing delay diagnosis and proper treatment. Prevention requires collective action: keep drains clear, cover water containers, sleep under nets, seek testing for fevers, and complete prescribed courses. Government should strengthen sanitation, expand net access and testing, and bolster community education and vector-control.

article.articleHeadline: A study tracking cholera transmission networks in Africa and determining the chances of its spread between countries - Step News Agency
article.articleSummary: An integrated genomic-epidemiologic study of cholera in Africa analyzes 1762 genomes from 36 countries (1989–2023) and surveillance data from 45 nations (1970–2023). Published in Science, it identifies regional transmission units: two in West Africa and neighbors, a central-east-southern corridor, and a southern cluster; broader epidemiology supports two networks (West Africa and central-to-southern Africa). Transmission declines with distance (88% per 1000 km), but within-unit spread is ~13.5 times higher than between units. AFR10 and AFR9 lineages account for ~46% of Africa’s cholera cases since 1970 (~2.4 million). A Hidden Markov Model combines clinical and genomic data to estimate spread during sampling gaps. Simulations (2000 imports per country) show within-unit outbreaks ~10x likelier in a year; Ghana could seed 4.69 more West African countries, Nigeria 4.33, Cameroon 0.58. Implication: prioritize vaccination in Mozambique if Angola’s outbreak spreads, reflecting network connectivity. Limitations include sampling bias and reliance on suspected cases.

article.articleHeadline: Zambia Plans 20 Million-Dose Cholera Vaccine Plant Under Agreement with Chinese Firm
article.articleSummary: Zambia's IDC and China's Jijia International Medical Technology signed a US$24.13 million joint venture to establish ZAMVAX Limited, a vaccine-fill-and-finish facility in Lusaka's South Multi-Facility Economic Zone with capacity to produce up to 20 million oral cholera vaccine doses annually using imported bulk antigen. The broader project totals about US$213 million, with a second phase to introduce local antigen production and possible expansion into pediatric and animal vaccines; IDC will hold 60% and Jijia 40%. The first phase covers filling, finishing, packaging and quality control, not full local vaccine production. Groundbreaking is expected soon; financing, site prep, tech agreements, workforce development and regulatory approvals will follow. The plan addresses vaccine-supply vulnerabilities noted during the Nov 2025 cholera outbreak (957 cases, 20 deaths by Feb 2026). IDC/Jijia will provide technology transfer and training, creating skilled jobs and opportunities for local suppliers.
